Accessible chromatin of chronically stimulated CD8 T cells: an Ep300/Runx3/Eomes enhancer landscape spanning progenitor and terminal exhaustion genes

Peaksexample_tex_peaks_mm10.bed (351)
Genomemm10
AssayATAC-seq
Target-
Cell typeCD8 T cells
Conditionchronic LCMV clone 13 infection, day 30
Modeagent (Claude (Claude Code session acting as the agent))
SummaryHypothesesInterpretationResultsBrowserReferencesMethodsLog
Known biology provided

Synthetic example. Peaks from chronically stimulated (exhausted-like) CD8 T cells. Exhaustion is driven by TOX and NR4A family factors downstream of persistent TCR/NFAT signalling, while TCF1 (Tcf7) marks the progenitor-exhausted subset. We want to know which pathways and transcription factors these peaks point to.

Expected genes: Tox, Pdcd1, Havcr2, Entpd1, Tcf7, Cd160

Expected TFs: Nfatc1, Nr4a1, Batf, Tcf7

Summary

The 351 peaks are clean, narrow ATAC-like regions [E1]. 79% lie away from promoters, so this is mostly an enhancer landscape [E2]. Peak-linked genes are strongly enriched for T-cell differentiation and activation terms, in both promoter and distal peaks [E4]. All six expected exhaustion genes (Tox, Pdcd1, Havcr2, Entpd1, Tcf7, Cd160) carry peaks, often several each [E22].

In public ChIP-seq from immune cells, the peaks overlap most with Ep300, the cohesin subunit Smc1a, the CD8 T-cell transcription factors Bcl11b, Tbx21, Eomes and Runx3 (with its partner Cbfb), and the signalling factors Stat3 and NF-kB Rela [E16]. That pattern points to active T-cell enhancers. Batf is supported twice: its public ChIP-seq overlaps these peaks (rank 20) [E16] and its target genes overlap the peak-linked promoter genes (93% vs 56% background) [E8]. Tcf7 targets overlap less (89% vs 66%) [E7].

The expected NFAT and NR4A factors are not recovered by motifs or public co-binding [E22]. No motif passes FDR [E5, E6], so regulator calls here rest on public co-binding, not sequence.

Important: the user notes describe this as a synthetic example built around exhaustion genes. The pathway and signature enrichments are therefore partly circular and should not be read as discovery.

Hypotheses and next experiments

H1. The distal peaks are Ep300/cohesin-marked active enhancers bound by Runx3 and Eomes, which together maintain the accessible exhaustion landscape.

medium

Evidence: E2, E16

Test: Runx3 and Eomes CUT&RUN plus H3K27ac in chronic (cl13) vs acute (Arm) d30 CD8 T cells; then CRISPRi of the top shared distal peaks near Pdcd1 and Havcr2 with a PD-1/Tim-3 flow readout.

H2. Batf is a direct regulator of the promoter-proximal part of this program even though its motif is not enriched in these sequences.

medium

Evidence: E8, E16, E5

Test: Batf CUT&RUN in Tex cells to test direct binding at the 67 overlapping promoters; ATAC-seq of Batf-deficient vs control P14 cells in clone 13 infection.

H3. The peak set is a mixture of progenitor (TCF1+) and terminal exhausted chromatin rather than one state.

medium

Evidence: E4, E9, PMID:32396847

Test: Sort Ly108+CX3CR1- progenitor and Tim-3+CX3CR1- terminal Tex cells and run ATAC separately; test whether progenitor-signature peaks (Tcf7, Sell, Ccr7) and terminal-signature peaks (Havcr2, Entpd1, Cd160) split by subset.

Interpretation

What the peaks are

QC found no duplicates, off-chromosome contigs or width outliers (median 350 bp) [E1]. With a -1000/+500 bp promoter window chosen for sharp ATAC peaks, 71 peaks are promoter-proximal, 277 distal and 3 more than 100 kb from any TSS [E2]. The median distance to the nearest TSS is about 13 kb [E2]. Most signal is therefore in introns and intergenic regions (25.6% and 36.8%) [E2]. That is typical of T-cell ATAC landscapes, where the state-specific changes are concentrated in enhancers. The exhaustion field describes Tex cells as having a distinct chromatin landscape from effector and memory cells [PMID:31207603].

Pathways and cell-state signatures

Promoter- and distal-linked genes both enrich for lymphocyte and T-cell differentiation (GO BP padj 1e-23 promoter, 3e-16 distal) and for Hallmark TNFA/NF-kB, IL2-STAT5 and allograft-rejection programs [E4].

All three user signatures are enriched: terminal exhaustion most strongly at promoters (padj 2e-28), with progenitor and effector-like signatures in both groups [E4]. So the accessible landscape covers genes of both the TCF1+ progenitor and the terminal exhausted states. The field describes these as distinct, developmentally linked subsets [PMID:30778252, PMID:32396847].

The pathway networks collapse the redundant GO terms into five modules: lymphocyte differentiation, adaptive immune response, regulation of hemopoiesis, alpha-beta T-cell differentiation, and leukocyte cell-cell adhesion [E4]. In the gene-pathway network, Bcl6, Ccr7, Ifng, Lef1 and Tbx21 each sit in all five module-lead pathways [E4]. So the enrichment is driven by core T-cell fate regulators and effector genes, not by one narrow pathway.

The top individual ImmuneSigDB hits are generic activation contrasts from B cells, CD4 T cells and neutrophils [E4]. The network does separate out one CD8-specific module, however: four naive vs effector/memory CD8 signatures led by KAECH_NAIVE_VS_DAY15_EFF_CD8_TCELL_DN (best padj 1.4e-12) [E4]. That supports an effector/memory-differentiated CD8 identity, though not exhaustion specifically.

Among the user signatures, Cx3cr1 and Gzmb are shared by the terminal and effector-like signatures [E4]. That is consistent with the overlap between terminal-exhausted and effector-like states.

Candidate regulators

  • Ep300 + cohesin (Smc1a): the strongest and most reproducible public overlap (Ep300 significant in 75/125 immune experiments) [E16]. This marks the peaks as active enhancers and is not tied to one cell state.
  • Bcl11b, Tbx21, Eomes, Runx3/Cbfb: CD8 T-cell TFs whose public peaks overlap these regions in CD8/NK/T cells [E16]. They are the best-supported sequence-specific candidates.
  • Stat3 and Rela (NF-kB): signal-responsive factors, consistent with the Hallmark TNFA/NF-kB and IL2-STAT5 programs [E16, E4].
  • Batf: no motif signal [E5, E6], but its public ChIP-seq co-binds these peaks (rank 20; 16/45 experiments) [E16, E22] and its target genes overlap the peak-linked promoter genes strongly (p = 4e-12) [E8].
  • Tcf7: not among the top 25 co-binding factors [E22], with modest target overlap [E7]. Expected if only part of the population is progenitor-like.
  • Not supported: Nfatc1 and Nr4a1 [E22]. TOX itself has no public immune ChIP-seq in the top hits, so TOX involvement cannot be tested with these data.

Expression and public data

All 17 up- and 10 down-regulated genes in the user's table carry a linked peak. Peaks sit at genes going both up (Pdcd1, Tigit, Ctla4, Prdm1, Tox) and down (Bach2, Klf2, Tcf7) [E9]. With only 47 genes tested this is illustrative, not a genome-wide test [E9].

GEO has several directly comparable exhausted-CD8 chromatin datasets [E15]: 3D-genome studies of Tex cells with matched ATAC and CUT&RUN [GSE343748, GSE284090], a chromatin-hub study implicating Id proteins [GSE310322], and a Klf2 early-exhaustion ATAC set [GSE288039]. Any of these would be a natural overlap or replication set.

Caveats

  • Synthetic input: peaks were placed at preselected exhaustion and effector genes (user notes), so gene-set and signature enrichments are partly circular [E4].
  • No motif passed FDR in all or distal peaks [E5, E6]; regulator calls rely on overlap with public ChIP-seq, which reflects co-occupancy, not causality [E16].
  • ChIP-Atlas target lists cover more than half of all genes (13.8k Batf, 16.3k Tcf7 of 24.5k), so target-overlap tests have weak specificity [E7, E8].
  • The RNA-seq table has only 47 genes, so the integration is illustrative [E9].
  • Genes are linked to peaks by nearest TSS; distal peaks may regulate other genes.
  • GREAT region-based enrichment was not run (rGREAT unavailable in this R install).

Each result has an id (E1, E2, …) that the narrative cites. Tables are linked relative to this report.

Methods

Peaks were filtered to standard chromosomes, de-duplicated. Peaks were annotated with ChIPpeakAnno (v3.36.1) against TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene gene models: each peak was assigned its nearest gene by TSS distance, and all genes whose TSS window (-1000/+500 bp) overlapped the peak were recorded as promoter targets. Genomic-region distribution used assignChromosomeRegion and the TSS profile used binOverFeature. Over-representation of peak-linked genes was tested with clusterProfiler (v4.10.1) (GO via org.*.eg.db, KEGG, ReactomePA (v1.46.0), MSigDB via msigdbr (v10.0.2)) against all annotated genes as background, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Known-motif enrichment used monaLisa (v1.8.1) with JASPAR2020 CORE vertebrate PWMs on 200 bp windows centred on peaks, against a GC-matched random genomic background. Overlap with public ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq experiments was tested with ChIP-Atlas Enrichment Analysis (random-permutation background, Fisher's exact test, BH-adjusted). Known TF target genes were taken from ChIP-Atlas target-gene tables; overlap was assessed with a hypergeometric test. Differentially expressed genes were intersected with peak-linked genes; enrichment was assessed with a hypergeometric test over all tested genes. Related literature was retrieved from Europe PMC and related datasets from NCBI GEO. Analysis steps were selected and results interpreted by an LLM agent (Claude (Claude Code session acting as the agent)); all statistics come from the tools above and every claim in the narrative is linked to its source result.
